fun.reason: Hit rate of 0.58-0.69 hits per throw means most throws connect, which feels good, but 6.5 pity triggers and 15 comeback hits per 3v3 match show the game is propping itself up artificially.

fairness.reason: The left side wins 65% of engine 3v3 and 58.8% of 2v2 even though the opener is fixed, and 1v1 matchups range from 26% (knight vs skeleton) to 74%, so both the opener and the hero pick decide too much.

tension.reason: A strength gap of 1 gives 78% and a gap of 2 gives 93% (engine), so many matches are decided before they start, and comeback hits of 9-16 per match patch over a lost position rather than create close finishes.

pacing.reason: Team matches average 12.1 rounds (2v2) and 17.5 rounds (3v3) against 8.5 in 1v1; the 3v3 p10 of 16 rounds means even the fastest matches run very long.

team_play.reason: Only one thrower acts per team per round, so with 3 units each unit throws about once every 3 rounds, and the 'comeback_hits' stat (15 per 3v3 match) suggests the comeback rules do more work than positioning or focus-fire.

replayability.reason: Eight heroes with several lopsided matchups (knight beats only 2 of 7 others at over 50% vs skeleton: 26% win rate, skeleton wins 74%), and 'left_lead' hero win rates of 20% to 73% mean some picks are clearly worse.

top_weaknesses: Match length: 3v3 averages 17.5 rounds (p10 16, p90 19) and 2v2 12.1; without seconds per round this cannot reach 7 minutes unless each round is about 24 s (3v3), which is unrealistic with aiming and wind.
Opener advantage in the engine: red wins 65% in 3v3 and 58.8% in 2v2 with a fixed first team; the page sim shows 53.8% and 56.2%, so the two simulations also disagree by up to 11 points.

Hero matchup spread in 1v1: skeleton beats knight 73.7% (knight beats skeleton 26.3%), skeleton beats hunchback 65%; the knight has the highest hp (185) but the lowest 1v1 strength in the matrix against skeleton.

Strength-gap snowball: engine win rate is 78.3% at gap +1 and 92.9% at gap +2, and the page sim shows 4.5% at gap -2, so a small skill lead makes the match decided; the owner accepts skill gaps but the curve is steeper than the comeback rules suggest.

Comeback systems are very active: 6.5 pity triggers and 15.0 comeback hits per 3v3 match (9.0 and 4.7 in 2v2), and the pity stacks to +160% on top of an underdog bonus of up to +100% (max total 2.3x), so swings come from rules rather than skill.

Near-miss reach of 450 px with scale 0.9 means a ground hit up to 450 px away still deals up to 90% damage, which blurs the difference between a hit and a miss; hits_per_throw rises to 0.67-0.69 in 3v3.

Hero table spread: wizard has 124 hp with 33 dmg while knight has 185 hp with 21 dmg, hunchback has 19 dmg at 147 hp; hunchback left-lead win rate is 23.3% (page) and 40% (engine), so it is the weakest pick in team play.

The ramp does not start until round 13, yet 2v2 matches end at 12.1 rounds on average, so the ramp that should speed up long games almost never applies in 2v2, and in 3v3 it applies only for about 4-5 rounds.

to_reach_10.change: Cut team match length to a fixed round budget and assume a measured seconds-per-round value
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Target 3v3 at 9-10 rounds and 2v2 at 8-9 rounds, which at roughly 40-45 s per round gives about 7 minutes; measure real seconds per round first.
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Brings 7-minute matches within reach and keeps tension up because each throw matters more.
to_reach_10.risk: If real rounds take longer than 45 s, matches overshoot; the target must be recomputed once timing is measured.

to_reach_10.change: Lower team hp scale much further
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: hp_scale 2v2 from 0.9 to about 0.62 and 3v3 from 0.95 to about 0.52, aiming for 8-9 and 9-10 average rounds.
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Matches shorten by roughly 30-45%, since the 1v1 baseline is 8.5 rounds with full hp and 2-3 units share the damage.
to_reach_10.risk: Too little hp makes one lucky crit or ultimate decisive and weakens comebacks; hp_floor_hits of 2.5 should be kept so no unit dies in under 2.5 hits.

to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: ramp start_round from 13 to 6 (2v2) and 7 (3v3), per_round from 0.08 to 0.10, and lower round_cap to 14 (2v2) and 16 (3v3).
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Gives a hard ceiling near the target length and makes the ramp actually apply, since today 2v2 mean 12.1 is below the start round 13.
to_reach_10.risk: A strong ramp rewards whoever is ahead on hp when it kicks in, which increases snowballing.

to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Give the second team a small compensation: +8-10% first-round damage or a free supply crate for the second mover, tuned so the engine left win rate goes from 65% (3v3) and 58.8% (2v2) to 50-52%; or let the second team choose the target first.
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Removes the 15-point opener edge in 3v3 and makes results depend on play.
to_reach_10.risk: Over-correcting flips the advantage to the second mover; test with at least 240 matches per size and require the left win rate within 48-52%.

to_reach_10.change: Scale back the comeback systems and stop stacking them
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Cap pity at 0.8 (from 1.6) and per_miss at 0.2, max_total_multiplier from 2.3 to 1.6, near-miss reach from 450 px to 250 px and scale from 0.9 to 0.6.
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Comeback hits fall from 15 to about 6-8 per 3v3 match, so a hit means something and skill shows, while a trailing team still gets help.
to_reach_10.risk: Weaker help increases snowballing (gap +1 already gives 78%); watch the win rate at gap +1 and aim for about 65%.

to_reach_10.change: Fix the worst 1v1 matchups and the weak heroes
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Knight dmg from 21 to 24 and hp from 185 to 170; skeleton hp from 150 to 142; hunchback dmg from 19 to 23. Target every 1v1 pairing between 40% and 60% (today 26.3%-73.7%).
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Removes the skeleton-over-knight counter (73.7%) and lifts hunchback (23% left-lead win rate in the page sim), widening the usable hero pool.
to_reach_10.risk: Changing three heroes at once can create new outliers (wizard at 124 hp and 33 dmg is already close to the edge); rerun the 300-per-pairing matrix after each change.

to_reach_10.change: Let more than one unit act per round in teams
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Replace one thrower per team per round with every living unit throwing once per round, while cutting rounds to 5-6; or keep one thrower but with a bonus for the unit that did not throw last round.
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Each unit acts every round, so a 3v3 round count of about 6 gives the same number of throws as 18 today while feeling faster, and focus-fire and positioning start to matter.
to_reach_10.risk: Doubles or triples the damage per round and the time per round; the 7-minute budget must be recomputed.

to_reach_10.change: Align the two simulations and run team simulations
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Make the engine and page sims agree within 3 points (today 65.0% vs 53.8% left win rate in 3v3) and fill team_simulation_runs with at least 240 matches per size and per hero mix.
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Gives one trusted number set to tune against instead of two that disagree by about 11 points.
to_reach_10.risk: Without agreement every tuning decision is guesswork; fixing it first costs time.

seven_minute_plan.rounds_target: 3v3 about 10 rounds and 2v2 about 8 rounds, assuming about 40 s per round; recompute as 420 s divided by the measured seconds per round.
seven_minute_plan.hp_scale: 2v2 about 0.60 and 3v3 about 0.50, then adjust until the mean rounds hit the target; keep hp_floor_hits at 2.5.
seven_minute_plan.ramp_start_round: Round 6 for 2v2 and round 7 for 3v3, with per_round 0.10, so the ramp is active in the final third of every match.
seven_minute_plan.round_cap: 14 for 2v2 and 16 for 3v3 (from 24 and 28), so even the p90 match ends at the cap close to 9-10 minutes at most.
seven_minute_plan.reasoning: Today 2v2 averages 12.1 rounds and 3v3 17.5 rounds, 1.4x and 2.0x the 1v1 average of 8.5. At 40 s per round that is 8.1 and 11.7 minutes, so 3v3 is far over 7 minutes and 2v2 is slightly over. Cutting hp by 30-45% and starting the ramp inside the normal match length brings the average to 8-10 rounds; the 40 s per round is an assumption, not a measurement.

cannot_judge: How long a round really lasts in seconds (aiming, wind reading, animations), so the 7-minute target cannot be converted from rounds with confidence.
How human players behave: all matches are computer-controlled, so real aim quality, hero choice and risk-taking are unknown.
Whether the visuals, sounds, hit feedback and ultimates feel good, since only numbers are given.
How mixed-team hero synergies play out, because team_simulation_runs is empty and only the matrix of random-strength teams is available.
Why the engine and page simulations disagree (65.0% vs 53.8% left win in 3v3); the cause cannot be seen from the summary.
Whether the hidden random opponent strength matches what players meet in real matchmaking, so the strength-gap curves may not transfer.
How supply crates, the centre fence and wind affect outcomes, since none of them are broken out in the data.
